WWC single-case design standards screening check

Source: R/utils-wwc.R
wwc_design_check.Rd

Screens the phase structure of single-case data against the research design requirements and the risk-of-bias rules of the What Works Clearinghouse (WWC) Procedures and Standards Handbook, Version 5.0, and reports the highest research rating the data structure is eligible for. This is a screening aid, not an official WWC review: outcome validity, confounding factors, researcher control of the independent variable, and residual treatment effects are not assessed, and visual analysis by trained reviewers is still required.

Usage

wwc_design_check(
  data,
  design = detect_design_type(data),
  time_var = find_time_var(data),
  outcome_var = "outcome",
  intervention_goal = "increase",
  ioa_value = NULL,
  ioa_coverage = NULL,
  ioa_type = c("percentage", "kappa")
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with case, phase, time, and outcome columns.

design

Design type: "reversal", "changing_criterion", "multiple_baseline", "multiple_probe", "ab", or "alternating"; defaults to detect_design_type().

time_var

Time column; NULL uses row order.

outcome_var

Outcome column.

intervention_goal

"increase" or "decrease"; orients the baseline-trend and reversibility NAP.

ioa_value

Optional overall IOA value (proportion or percentage).

ioa_coverage

Optional proportion of data points with IOA (values above 1 are read as percentages); a value outside 0-1 after that scaling is an error.

ioa_type

"percentage" (minimum .80) or "kappa" (minimum .60).

Value

A list with rating (overall), reasons, experiments (one row per experiment or contrast with its rating and reasons), tiers (phase structure per tier), baseline_trend, reversibility, ioa (status and detail), design, and note.

Details

Common rules. Every design needs three attempts to demonstrate an effect at three different points in time. A phase with three or more data points and no within-phase variability counts toward the Meets Without Reservations data-point requirements. A design receives the highest rating any subset of it is eligible for, provided the subset still holds three demonstrations and compares only adjacent phases; extra phases or tiers with fewer data points do not lower the rating.

Reversal/withdrawal (each case is one experiment). At least two phases per condition, that is four alternating phases. Without Reservations: the initial baseline of the case has six or more points, also when the qualifying window starts at a later phase, and the other phases five or more; With Reservations: three or more points in two phases per condition. The check searches every window of four consecutive alternating baseline/intervention phases. Reasons name the phases that pass only through zero variability.

Changing criterion (each case is one experiment). The reversal rules apply with every baseline, intervention, or criterion change counted as a phase change, so three changes are required; maintenance and generalization phases are not criterion changes, and a series without a baseline phase does not meet standards. When the data carry a numeric criterion, crit, criterion_level, or criterion_value column, phases are split on phase label and criterion value together, so each criterion change opens a phase; a missing criterion value carries the last one forward within the phase.

Multiple baseline and multiple probe (each study is one experiment). At least six phases, i.e. three tiers with a baseline to intervention change, and at least three distinct intervention onsets. Without Reservations: first baseline of six or more points in each tier and later phases of five or more; With Reservations: three phases per condition with three or more points. Concurrence: every tier has baseline data before the first intervention onset, and every tier still in baseline has data at or after each earlier onset; vertical alignment is assumed from the shared time axis. Concurrence is judged across all tiers: a design that fails it is rated Does Not Meet WWC Standards, and no subset can restore the rating. Multiple probe designs add three rules: probes in the first three sessions (all three for Without, one common session for With), probes just before the onset (three consecutive for Without, at least one within the three prior sessions for With), and a probe for every untreated tier in the session another tier starts intervention. With design left at its default, a multiple baseline design with a baseline gap between sessions longer than the median session spacing of the same tier's intervention phase (baseline rows absent, as with planned probes) is reviewed as a multiple probe design. A row with an NA outcome is unplanned missing data and stays under the multiple baseline rules; pass design to override either reading. Concurrence is read strictly: a tier whose baseline data all end before an earlier tier's onset fails, even when it is measured again later in intervention.

Combination designs. When a reversal or changing-criterion design has three or more tiers, the first baseline-intervention phases of the tiers are also screened as a multiple baseline design within each study; when it rates higher than every tier of that study, a row naming the multiple baseline reading is added.

A two-phase AB design is screened under the same rules, so AB tiers sharing one onset fail the distinct-onset requirement.

Alternating treatments (each case and pair of conditions is one contrast). At least five points per condition for Without and four for With Reservations, and no more than two consecutive points of one condition within the rapidly alternating phase. A leading baseline of more than two points is set aside from the alternation, also when the baseline condition recurs within it. A final run of more than two points is a separate phase, exempt from the consecutive-point rule and left out of the point counts, only when it continues the most successful intervention: a condition with a recognised intervention, maintenance, or generalization role (see phase_role(); single letters C-H also count as interventions, other unrecognised labels such as "Ctl" are never exempt) whose alternating phase mean is strictly the highest of all conditions, ties excluded and baseline included (the lead baseline enters with its own mean when it does not recur in the alternation; lowest when intervention_goal = "decrease"); any other final run stays in the alternation. Trailing maintenance or generalization phases whose labels never alternate are left out of the alternating comparison but still count as phases for the IOA rule. When the baseline condition does not recur in the alternation, the single lead baseline is compared with each intervention-role condition of the alternating phase as its own contrast, under the same data-point rule (five points per condition for Without, four for With); the consecutive-point rule applies to the alternating condition only. Unrestricted random assignment of condition order is also exempt but cannot be detected from the data.

Risk of bias. Designs other than alternating treatments that are eligible for Without Reservations are rated With Reservations at best when the initial baseline shows a therapeutic trend or reversibility is incomplete. Baseline trend compares the last three baseline points with all earlier baseline points (nonoverlap of all pairs, NAP); a baseline with zero variability and three or more points meets the rule. Reversibility compares the initial baseline with each return-to-baseline phase of a reversal or changing-criterion design. NAP of .85 or less meets each rule; NAP is oriented by intervention_goal. For multiple baseline designs every baseline in the qualifying subset must meet the trend rule.

Interassessor agreement (IOA). At least .80 for percentage agreement or .60 for Cohen's kappa across phases and cases, collected in each phase and for at least 20\ from a numeric column whose name contains ioa, agreement, kappa, or reliab (one value per session with agreement data, NA otherwise; values above 1 are read as percentages), or from ioa_value and ioa_coverage. IOA below the minimum fails the outcome reliability standard and caps the rating at Does Not Meet; without either source IOA is reported as not assessed. An ioa_value without ioa_coverage or an IOA column checks the value only: coverage is reported as not assessed (status "partially assessed") and does not cap the rating. The rule that every phase carries IOA data applies only when the IOA column is the value source, not when ioa_value is supplied. The handbook asks for IOA in each phase without limiting it to the compared phases, so lead, final, maintenance, and generalization runs of an alternating design are each a phase for that rule.

Phase labels without a known role (see phase_role()) take their roles from first appearance in time, with a warning.

Study-level rating. The overall rating is the highest rating among the experiments.

Next steps. Findings that meet standards proceed to effect size estimation; the WWC computes a design-comparable effect size for reversal, multiple baseline, and multiple probe designs with three or more cases, implemented in the scdhlm package. Studies that meet standards can proceed to that design-comparable BC-SMD, which scdbayes estimates in a Bayesian model (bc_smd_bayes()) and pools with a Bayesian meta-analysis (meta_bayes()); scdhlm/metafor scripts are optional frequentist comparisons. scdbayes does not compute the within-case SMD, which is biased under autocorrelation.

Examples

d <- data.frame(case = "P1", time = 1:21,
                phase = rep(c("A", "B", "A", "B"), c(6, 5, 5, 5)),
                outcome = c(3, 4, 3, 4, 3, 4, 8, 9, 8, 9, 8,
                            4, 3, 4, 3, 4, 9, 8, 9, 8, 9))
wwc_design_check(d)$rating
#> [1] "Meets WWC Standards Without Reservations"
